newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa heads down at noon, activity stalled.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa heads down at noon, activity stalled.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures were virtually at a standstill by the midsession on Wednesday, a move that startled traders, and prices were broadly lower as expected.
"It's incredible," said one. "After the good moves in the recent days, the market is suddenly dead. May be the people are watching (the) Wimbledon (tennis championships). "
Volume was just a paltry 477 lots at midday compared with 4,131 lots at lunch on Tuesday.
The main interest this morning was the light liquidation of the benchmark September contract, traders said.
September finished the morning trade 12 stg down at 1,146 stg a tonne while December shed 13 at 1,150.
The September contract closed at the contract's high of 1,160 stg on Tuesday although it failed to match the June 1996 high of 1,172 based on the second-month continuation chart.

The second quarter European cocoa grind data due to be released later this week or early next week. Analysts said the figures were expected to show a mixed trend and traders said they would have little impact on the market.
